payload.name: Enumeration search for which-achievement questions
payload.description: When a question asks which achievements, records, career-highs, or performances someone achieved, treat it as an exhaustive enumeration and search each possible subcategory.
content: When a question asks 'Which <achievement-type> did <entity> achieve?' (e.g., which career-high performances, records, awards, milestones), treat it as an enumeration request whose answer may span multiple distinct items in separate memories.

Do not finalize an answer after the first retrieved item; run additional searches using terms for each plausible subcategory of the achievement type (e.g., for career-high performances: points, assists, rebounds, blocks; for awards: specific award names) and synonyms for 'highest'/'best'.

Check sufficiency after each search: if new searches return distinct items, continue; only answer when additional searches yield no new items, and include all retrieved memories that match the asked category.

solves: The access agent answered an enumerative 'which achievements/performances' question after retrieving only one of two expected career-high items, because it treated the question as a single-item lookup. Reusable guidance is to treat such 'which' questions as exhaustive enumeration requests across subcategories, and to keep searching until no new items appear. This applies to any future question asking which records, awards, or best performances someone achieved, independent of the specific domain.
